The basis for passing this decision was the law on taxation and contributions which regulated the taxation matters, and it further stated that the income tax was levied by the municipal organs and that the municipal assembly decided on the income tax. Based on the law on taxation, the draft of this decision was prepared and the Crisis Staff adopted this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The duty to pay these taxes, did it apply to the people who lived in the municipality -- on the territory of the municipality or those who lived abroad? Please take a look at this decision and answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty to pay taxes specified in this decision applied to persons who lived abroad in view of the fact that the National Assembly of Republika Srpska decided that general call for mobilisation need not be answered by all citizens, that means that those who lived abroad did not have to respond to the mobilisation call-up. Therefore, this created legal grounds for having these people who lived abroad contribute to the effort in a certain way, since the expenses were very high, these people were asked to help in some way and this is how they participated in the entire effort. This decision -- or rather, this source of revenue was used by the municipality for a very brief period of time, because very soon thereafter the government passed its own decree specifying that this type of income was not in the competencies of municipality any more but rather in the competencies of the republic because the government had taken over the entire obligation to fund the army, police, education, and those institutions that were funded by the government. These funds were now provided by the government budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Before the witness goes on, perhaps he could clarify what he means by "abroad" here. Does he mean outside the Republika Srpska as in abroad or some other -- or something else? It could be important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Or when he was talking about people working abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Abroad. What does abroad mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you heard the question. Can you please clarify. What did that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That meant people residing in Germany, Austria, Italy, France, any other country outside of the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now let's see what the factual situation was. What was ethnic background of taxpayers that are mentioned here? So in other words, who directed these funds?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Samac municipality it was the Serbs. There were a few Muslims, those that remained in Samac but had moved abroad were few. There were few such Muslims. And the Serbs constituted the majority, so therefore they were those who paid this tax. And now let me tell you how was this tax paid. It was paid when these people came back home. Then they would report to authorities and pay the tax.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you didn't have accounts in foreign banks where these taxes could be paid into, but rather, when these people came back home, then the tax could be collected; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because these accounts in foreign banks would be useless to us. We had no payment system with other countries. Therefore, this tax was collected only once these people returned back to Samac. This is when the decision on collection of these taxes would be handed in to them, and then once they paid it, they would be issued a receipt. When these people left the country and crossed the border, they had to show the receipt to financial inspectors or customs officers at the border crossing, who would then allow them to leave the country without hinderance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit P110 and P111, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a brief comment, please. This is a decision that you've already explained. Please tell me, you've seen this decision before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you a candidate for president of the executive council as well in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. However, I heard that I had been. I heard it from Milan, that I had been a candidate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you hear how the procedure on appointment went? Was there any discussion, deliberation, or was the person simply appointed without any discussion taking place prior to that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from Milan Simic that there had been a deliberation, that the members of the Crisis Staff discussed his and my candidacy. I don't know whether there were any other candidates. And according to him, Blagoje Simic favoured my candidacy; however, after the voting procedure, he was appointed. And after he told me that, I said that that was probably the reason I was appointed vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you put the exhibit on the ELMO, P111.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On that same day this decision was passed appointing you vice-president of the executive council; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now P112, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this is the third document dated 30th of May, 1992, please tell me whether you have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps what professionals or professional service prepared this document to be adopted?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was prepared by us, or rather, it was prepared by our professional staff at the executive council, because we knew this subject matter very well. We knew what "executive council" meant and what "administrative organ" meant. And this was all pursuant to the law on state administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So based on this decision, various secretariats were formed of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This created a legal basis for the executive bodies to be filled in accordance with this decision. And this implied the forming of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now, please, Exhibit D43/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell me whether you've seen this document before, and if you did, do you know anything specific about this document, based on your experience?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document before. This is the first time that I see it. But it reminds me of the things that we did before the war, because there was a plan in the municipality for defence or a plan for extraordinary circumstances. And each secretariat of the executive council or the executive body had its own plan. This reminds me of someone who used to work in the Defence Ministry, or in the Territorial Defence headquarters, because it seems to be a person who is an expert who knew quite well to set down the basic postulates and then based on them, plans were supposed to be made at the level of the secretariats or the executive organs. It seems to me that this is a plan made by the Croat side, by the HDZ, because I can see Mato Madzarevic here, who is the Secretary for the Economy and that was the most important plan in the economy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I object to further evidence on this. This is pure speculation on a document that he has never seen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, could you please tell me, what do you base your conclusion on? And you say you haven't seen this document before. Could you use the pointer and tell us where you see these names and why is it that you interpret this document in this way. Where did you get this conclusion from?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I said I never saw this document before, but it's clear -- it states here clearly that the balance of the required funds use existing documents of the municipal assembly in the possession of Mato Madzarevic. Mato Madzarevic was the economy secretary at the municipal assembly, carrying out of regular programmed tasks from -- of the HDZ, that's the Croatian Democratic Council. I also saw the term here "Stozar," headquarters, which is a purely Croatian term.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D49/1, please. Excuse me, Mr. Usher. What is the number of that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What exhibit document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is the exhibit, the number? Because there is some -- some --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, my mistake in my -- sorry, 44. My mistake. I do apologise. It's a problem in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, who prepared this decision, first of all, if you know, and what was the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat for Economic Affairs apprised the situation out in the field, and they reviewed the situation with petrol and they proposed to the executive council to suggest to the Crisis Staff to restrict petrol consumption, since there was a shortage of it. It was to be reduced, the use, to the lowest possible level, and that is how this decision came about, restricting petrol use to 10 litres a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this decision affect all the citizens of Samac, regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes, whoever had a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit P -- sorry, D45/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell us the point of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was logical, since it was war, for catering businesses and restaurants not to work. So the Secretariat for Economy, or the executive council, proposed to the Crisis Staff to close down all such facilities. An additional motive was to prevent armed people from using such facilities because it might lead to all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the aim was to prevent incidents from taking place, since it was a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D61/1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who wrote this information?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This memo was written by the coordinator or the director of the Pik Samac enterprise. This is already 1993, so he's informing us that he has problems with members of the army who without control and without permission are entering their premises, their property, and are cutting down -- these are units from Krajina who were located near this area, and they are cutting down timber and taking it to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who is this memo addressed to?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For our information, so to the president of the executive council, to the president of the municipal assembly, to the chief for economic affairs, to the chief for defence, and also to the chief of the Public Security Station and to the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Regarding these kinds of incidents, was anything done either by the executive council, the municipal assembly, or any of the executive bodies? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Certain steps were taken in the appropriate domains. This question was something that was dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was any kind of protest lodged with the military authorities regarding these events?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that a meeting of the executive council was devoted to this memo, and I think a protest was written to the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade, i.e., to the 5th Tactical Group which was billeted in this area of responsibility, on the territory of our municipality. The protest was sent to Colonel Djurkic, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what is this 5th Tactical Group? What was its area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that kind of military information, but this was a formation of the 1st Krajina Corps, commanded by General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D64/1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you know and in view of item 2 of this conclusion, or paragraph 2, and the entire conclusion as such, could you please give us a very brief commentary, what was the purpose of this decision, what was it all about?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The War Presidency discussed the infrastructure in the town and its condition, and their assessment was, since we didn't have a construction company of our own, that it was necessary as soon as possible to set up such a company, which could then set about the reconstruction and rebuilding and repair of the infrastructure. So the executive council in accordance with relevant laws about the registering of enterprises, it was asked to provide the documents and secure the investment funds in order -- investment capital in order to establish such a company, which would then operate in the territory of our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about whether this process of repair of the infrastructure was something that would apply only to the damaged property of Serbs, or did it apply to damaged property of all ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A shell hit a building that was inhabited not only by Serbs but Muslims and Croats, still had to be repaired. So this reconstruction and repair was something that applied to the property of all, Serbs, Muslims, and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So there was no ethnic discrimination in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit D71/1, 72, and 73/1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Mr. Lukic, and then we will have completed with this set of questions. Please take a look at all three documents so that we can cover them as quickly as possible. So take a look at all three of them and tell us very briefly what you can about this because all of these decisions were passed in the month of May. What do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of our municipality, there were very many farms, raising cattle, poultry, pigs, and so on. And this deals with farms that had been inhabited and that did not have food. Therefore, the Crisis Staff decided to take the food or the feed from the agricultural concern and to deliver it to these farmers so that they can complete the cycle that they had started.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just take a brief look at these names. Do you know any of these people? Do you know what their ethnicity is?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Djosic [phoen] Pero is a Croat from Zasavica; Senjic Juro, also a Croat; Zasavica as well; Dunjic Mato is a Croat from Donji Hasici. All of them are Croats. But there had been decisions of this nature pertaining to Serbs as well, because everybody had problems, those who possessed farms, to procure cattle feed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So there was no discrimination based on ethnic origin, was there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't. This confirms that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now we would like to have, Madam Registrar, D11/2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we have a rare occasion to have a lawyer for a witness and especially somebody with such extensive experience, although we did have Mr. Tihic testify here, who's a lawyer, but I don't think we could have asked him this question -- therefore, in view of that, I will ask you a few questions and will require you to give us a legal commentary regarding these decrees passed by Republika Srpska. Some of these decrees pertain to your area of expertise, and then I will ask you some additional questions. If I'm not mistaken, this first decree -- well, just please read it out.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decree on --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer. And interpreters would like to stress that we do not have copies of these documents in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the interpreters don't have those copies. So when the witness is asked to read, he should read very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. In fact, we could put the -- the English version maybe on the ELMO just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before Mr. Pantelic starts, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He introduced the witness a moment ago as someone as a lawyer apparently with the expertise to comment on these particular provisions. My memory of the witness's curriculum vitae was he graduated -- sorry, he graduated some 20 years ago but has only been a lawyer since this year, I think it was, recently admitted to the bar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just querying the expertise to comment on these particular provisions, whether it's a constitutional expertise or some sort of working one or -- on what basis is he providing this running commentary of the laws of Republika Srpska, which on their face, I would submit, speak for themselves?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is aware that this witness is not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He is a fact witness who happens to be a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. In fact, just to clarify, a word "lawyer" in our language means, well, a person who graduated from law school but without bar exams. So he's not practicing lawyer in terms of western standards. And the question for this witness is very simple. He will not go into the interpretation -- legal interpretation of certain documents. He will speak only from his professional position as an official in the municipal authorities, executive board, and specifically limited to the part of legislation which was implemented within the municipality but which was initially adopted by the government of Republika Srpska. So it's on a daily basis his area of interest and professional work. So I would be limited -- I will be limiting only to that, to that level, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution doesn't object to the witness as a fact witness commenting on the practical implementation of the law in Bosanski Samac, but we do object to his interpreting the law as he goes, because that's not what he's here for.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I clarified that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You have. Mr. Pantelic clarified that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, this is a decree on organising and implementing the work obligation for defence requirements; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During your career and on your job, did you have any contact with this decree?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In very basic terms, since we will have other witnesses testifying about this, please tell us, what was the role of executive organs in a municipality when it came to links with the Ministry of Defence and the government of Republika Srpska in matters that are regulated by this decree? Just very briefly. We don't need to go into details. Just tell us how that mechanism operated.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government wanted to regulate the work obligation in a uniform manner, or rather, they wanted to regulate the relationship between the civilian organs and the Ministry of Defence. What does this practically mean? In my service, Internal Revenue Agency, I needed somebody to work as a bookkeeper. I, as the supervisor of that agency, would send a request to the office of the Ministry of Defence to issue a work obligation for that person. If that person already had a military obligation or was serving in the army, then I would ask the Ministry of Defence to dismiss him and appoint him to work in my agency. And if that person did not have a military obligation, then the Ministry of Defence would assign that person to work in my Internal Revenue Agency and that would be his work obligation. Or let me give you another example: If the company for water supply and sewage needed professionals, then the director of that company would, through the executive council, send a request to the Secretariat for National Defence to place those individuals in the water supply company as part of their work obligation. Another example would be that that person once appointed in a certain company, enterprise, or agency would then be issued a decision specifying that that was part of that person's work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now let's see what remuneration for that kind of work was. How did this process look like? I assume that people were compensated for their work. They received a salary.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in the beginning that funds were allocated from the budget for work obligation. Coordinator of an enterprise would deliver a list of his or her employees, and then the executive council would approve and then transfer the funds needed through the payment agency into the bank, and then these employees would be able to collect their salary at the bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please give us a comment of Article 8 of this decree.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, just give us your comment. How was this implemented in the territory of Samac municipality? I mean, Article 8.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military in its logistics had certain requirements which needed to be carried out with the participation of a large number of people. They had their combat tasks, and then they would send to the Ministry of Defence a request asking that a certain number of individuals be placed at the disposal of a certain brigade in order to carry out certain tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And these work platoons, were they in fact created pursuant to the work obligation and to the matters mentioned in Article 8?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were special units that carried out work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And finally, please comment on Article 2. Were you personally also covered by this article?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree copied the text from the law on defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the pre-war Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I told you that my war assignment was to serve as director of Internal Revenue Agency in the municipal assembly. That means that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I assume that pertained to other officials in the municipal administration as well, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it pertained to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Now I would like to turn to a different area that also has to do with the war situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You may, Mr. Usher, please, put B/C/S version in front of the witness and English translation on the ELMO in order to help our friends from the Translation Unit.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but the beginning of this decision is missing. I only have the ending of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It would be good to have it in transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The reason there are no numbers is because speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was, just for the record, D12/2. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your work, have you come across this decision?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I am particularly interested in your comment based on your practical, personal experience in application of this decision and Article 1 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Article 1 says that "This decision shall establish uniform tasks and activity that is shall be conducted by the executive committees of municipal assemblies of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina through the Secretariat for National Defence and the Secretariat for the Economy, and directors of enterprises, managerial and other organs and organisations, for the purposes of the functioning and protection of economic and other capacities and material goods."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And how did this look on the ground in Samac when it came to the executive organs of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our Secretariat for Economy cooperated with the Secretariat for Defence. Through the Crisis Staff they appointed coordinators, and then coordinators requested that certain number of people be given to them for work obligation in order to preserve the property of those enterprises in which they served as coordinators and in order to make sure that those companies that needed to work in wartime started working.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 2, item 1 of this decision says what? Please tell us, what did this pertain to? I mean, Article 2, item 1.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The complete physical security of production capacities and facilities --"

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you don't need to read this out to us. Just give us a brief commentary on how this looked on the ground. What did you have to do pursuant to this provision?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that the Crisis Staff had passed a decision on prevention of plundering. The Crisis Staff appointed coordinators in enterprises. The Secretariat for Economy in cooperation with the Ministry of Defence called up a certain number of persons who worked in these enterprises as part of their work obligation. So these are the steps that had been taken in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Item 2 of this article, please tell us what was the objective of item 2 in relation to the property that needed to be protected. Very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose was to protect property. Now, what did this actually mean? Since Samac was shelled daily --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you, Mr. Lukic. It's time for our break. I think we will continue in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is it time for a break, Your Honour? And I don't know. Do we have 20 minutes' break, or what is the schedule for today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break until 18.05.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, before the break, we were --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit D12/2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were talking about Article 2.2, talking about the relocation of production facilities. What happened in Samac? How did it function then? What measures were undertaken there in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff passed a decision and imposed it on the executive Secretariat for the Economy, which coordinated the companies which were in charge of supplying the population in the area of our municipality to draft a plan of activities and measures to dislocate certain production facilities of particular significance. Primarily this concerned the ready-made product, the semi-finished goods, and our company, that is, the coordinator for our company, drafted a plan along the following lines: In Serbia, that is, in Stara Pazova, it registered our company, that is, Samcanka Stara Pazova company, in which there was a warehouse and to which this facility was dislocated. And this was done for the following reason: At that time every day several times every day there was shelling of the town and especially of the industrial area, the health centre, the hospital, and shells fell from the direction of Croatia, Domaljevac, Orasje. A lot of property was destroyed as a result of that. Let me just give you an example: The livestock on the farms all died as a result of stress due to detonations, and that is why the livestock had to be taken out - we're talking about cattle - and when the cattle was transported to Serbia and taken to the slaughterhouse, a problem arose, with the acceptance of that cattle. I don't -- I'm not an expert, but that cattle had stains all over their carcasses as a result of the shock that it had sustained. So the coordinator in charge of the supply of the population made a list, together with the coordinators for other companies, the list consisting of the most vital capacities. And together with them, they made an estimate as to what needed to be preserved and prevented from shelling by way of dislocating those facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what about the products in the furniture factory? What happened to those?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their destiny was the same as the destiny of the products in the glass factory, in the boiler factory, in other factories. So all of these products were inflammable, and it took very little for them to catch fire, so all of these had to be dislocated. In the furniture factory, a machine which was worth about a million German marks burnt down as a result of shelling. The computer system of the machine burnt down, so the machine was destroyed. We had not been able to dislocate that machine before that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who was the owner of all these factories and all of these production facilities? Were these private factories? Who was their owner?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were socially-owned or state-owned factories. In Samac at the time there were no private factories of this type and of such a grand scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, in terms of your questions concerning the factory and then the other computer system of a machine burning down. The translation says of the answer with respect to those properties that they had to be dislocated. It doesn't make much sense to me. Does the witness mean that they had to be relocated, rather than dislocated? That's line 25 on page 61 and page 62, line 4.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Relocated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just one more question: Was Samac municipality in charge of appointing managerial staff in these factories, given the fact that it was its owner? So was it also in charge of managing these factories in that way?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the municipality was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With regard to Article 3 of this decision, what was the role of the non-mobilised people in terms of their work obligations? So what does that article mean?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that the government didn't want the factories to come to a standstill, that they had to continue producing in order to produce new, added value, and that is why the Secretariat for National Defence and the responsible command showed more understanding for the work obligation and assigning people for work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there an automatic procedure for those who were not mobilised to give them work obligation in certain factories or in certain facilities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they worked in a particular company or in a particular factory, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have -- thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have Exhibit D13/2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly with regard to this order issued by the government. Under item 2, did work obligation apply to the refugees in the territory of Samac? Were they also obliged to carry out some duties?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the able-bodied men who were not mobilised had work obligation, so there were no exceptions and both the domestic local population and all the others had the same obligation if they at the time resided in the territory of a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In accordance with this order, item 5, who were the ones who held the highest responsibilities in the companies, or the acting directors in the companies? For example, in Samac, who were the acting directors in the companies in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most responsible ones were the president of the Crisis Staff, obviously, the president of the executive council, the Secretary for Economy, and directors of the companies or the coordinators for those companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D14/2. It is not translated -- no, no, no. D15. Sorry, my mistake. This part was not translated, so I will not go into this issue. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have your very brief comment of this decision. Did this decision also apply to the municipal organs in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the amounts were not the same. I mean, the salaries. There was a different system of pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The budgetary resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D22/2. And I believe there are a certain number of these documents here, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand these are under seal, Your Honour. We certainly have a note -- we have a note to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If this is under seal, then I kindly ask to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, could you please tell me whether you ever saw this document in the course of your work or your agency.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. What is given here, we had to provide the funds. We had to pay that. This wasn't free. These persons received this for free, these goods that are stated here. But the centre for social work and the Red Cross only devised the criteria so that not everybody could receive this. Those who had a better standard of living or who were in the army or who were under work obligation and were receiving a salary could not receive this. And if persons were receiving a salary which was above the limit set here, they were not allowed to use this option. Only persons whose salaries fell below the standards or the criteria set here, they could receive milk and bread for free. So here it is stated who those persons are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And did this apply to all citizens of Samac, regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it applied to all the citizens in our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Exhibit D46/3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, can you please tell me -- you don't have to give me the exact figure, but could you please tell us approximately about the range in the number of refugees in Samac from 1992 -- from April 1992 and up to today or 1995, whatever is easier for you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have a report here from the 3rd of November, 1992, where the total number of refugees is 5.806. At the beginning of 1996 until March 1996, in the territory of our municipality there were about 10.500 refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell me, in view of the number of refugees that is mentioned, how did the municipal authorities - and I'm thinking of all the secretariats, the broad authorities - resolve the question of accommodation for all of these people? Please just give us a couple of examples. We don't have to spend a lot of time on this.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in May 1992 a whole village from Gradacac, which is a Muslim municipality, arrived to our municipality. Those were the citizens of the village of Srnice. It was about 400 families in all, so that we had to open a reception centre so that we could register them all in one place and then get them all settled. At one point, because there weren't enough empty abandoned houses, we had to locate them at the Kruskovo Polje, which is a Serb village near Gornja Slatina, so that we used the decision about surplus accommodation in order to settle all of those families, households. We did the same thing when persons came from Novi Grad and Donja Dubica. This is from Odzak. It's a Croat municipality. Those people were also received. And then a plan was made. The households were registered, and according to the number of persons in each household, those persons were placed in abandoned living quarters if there were such quarters. And if not, they were placed with local Serb families who had a surplus of living space, in accordance with the decision of the government of Republika Srpska. This happened with Drvar, Glamoc, Zavidovici, i.e., the citizens, the population from those places, Orasje, Sarajevo, Zenica, Kakanj, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge whether there were Serb refugees temporarily accommodated in the village of Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were refugees there from the territory of the municipality of Zavidovici. This is a Muslim municipality that is a part of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you happen to know, could you please tell us in which period did these refugees start arriving.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was maybe in 1992 or 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me something about the legal system or the court system which was operating in the municipality of Samac. What can you tell us about the competencies of the courts? We know that there was a court in Samac before 1992. How did the courts divide their territorial jurisdiction in the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samac as a municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina had a basic court, a first-instance court, and this court operated until the 17th of April, 1992. The judges of that court or some of them were transferred to the military court or the military prosecutor's office, so that in 1992 we were unable to organise the judiciary and its functioning, because we did not have a sufficient number of judges. Then the Ministry of Justice of the government of Republika Srpska expanded the territorial jurisdiction of the court in Modrica so that it started covering the territory of Samac municipality, Pelagicevo, and Srpsko Orasje. And this remains so until today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the court in Orasje was in charge of all civil and criminal cases, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In civil proceedings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about criminal cases?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both civil and criminal within the civil section.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, but what is the other section?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military one, which dealt with members of the army. They were under the jurisdiction of the military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There seems to be an error on the transcript. Mr. Pantelic asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- about the court in Modrica. And then a question about the court in Orasje. Is it the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, my friend. It's just a correction in the transcript. Instead of word "Orasje" on page 73, line 11, it should be "Modrica." Yes. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Usher, please. For the benefit of our friends from the Prosecution -- now we are going to discuss some documents from our exhibit list. And the first document is RP3. Yes. Ms. Registrar, these are the three copies for the Trial Chamber. So I don't know what would be appropriate. Maybe you can just follow the bundle of documents or can deliver them immediately. I don't know. What would be appropriate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The three bundles are -- contain all the exhibits you are going to discuss.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the Judges can be given a bundle each.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: These have be filed, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, they are filed, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have a list of these potential exhibits in my pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But now we are waiting for the -- for the exhibit number. I mean, after the discussion, and also if there is no objections from the Prosecution. So I would -- at this stage we could say that these are potential Defence exhibits. So you can take this first document, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I wanted to ask the Prosecution, since they already -- I take it they were given these copies. Has the exercise been completed where you have indicated to the Defence which ones you are objecting to, which ones you are not objecting to, or hasn't that been done?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The furthest we've got is that Mr. Pantelic has provided a list of documents which he wished to cross-examine on. Assuming that those are the ones that he wishes to tender, I can certainly indicate tomorrow whether we have any objections. I don't have any objections, of course, to Your Honours seeing them at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no indication as to whether Mr. Pantelic wishes to tender them at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also, Your Honour, if I may -- maybe we can go from -- on a case-by-case -- a document-by-document basis so we could immediately resolve the things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can discuss with your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good. So the first document is, as I said, RP3. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Maybe we could have the B/C/S version for the benefit of our clients on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, you have already spoke about various secretariats within the executive council. Now please give us a brief comment and tell us what this document deals with.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of these secretariats within the administration, within the executive council is the Secretariat for Social Services and Administration. And Article 1 specifies the responsibilities of this secretariat. It mostly deals with education and other social services that are not related to economy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So this is an integral part of the executive council of Samac municipality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's one of its organs. This is a secretariat which exists within the administration and within the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D74/1 and D74/1 ter, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the next document that I would like to discuss with this witness is RB4. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I need to know exactly what is the title, because all I have is "RB" and then I have a pile of two different documents. One is called "conclusions," and the other "decisions."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated 9th of June, 1992. It's a decision of executive board.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision on the business hours of the administrative organs, economic enterprises, and other institutions who had an approval to work in wartime. This was needed in order to have it regulated what were the business hours of various institutions, enterprises, and so on. This decision was passed by the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This pertains to the administrative organs. Article 1 specifies the business hours. Can you tell me what it says.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the business hours are from 8.00 in the morning till 6.00 p.m., which in case of members of the executive council was not true. They worked more than that, and the business hours that are specified here pertain to employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did it pertain to all employees regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know what were the business hours in some other enterprises, factory, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Business hours in factories were determined by their coordinator; however, it wasn't longer than the hours specified here in this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D75/1 and D75/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is RB11.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a very poor copy that we have in Serbian; however, just to give me your comment of this conclusion. But rather, first tell me when was this passed.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was passed in 1993. It's difficult to discern the date. I don't know if it was the 10th of February, 1993 or not. In Pelagicevo they did not have personnel in order to set up their electric power company; therefore, we tasked the director of our power company to establish contacts with their municipality, so that his employees, or rather, employees of our power electric -- electric power company also covered the jurisdiction of Pelagicevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, in 1992 and 1993, what was the situation like with electric power supply in Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first days of war, we had a disruption in the electric power supply. And thereafter for a long time we had no electricity whatsoever. Afterwards, when the power grid Bijeljina-Samac was established - and if I remember well, that was in late 1992, early 1993 - the power supply became more normal. However, we had certain restrictions in the number of hours during which we had electrical power.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please, for this exhibit if there is no objection from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again, no objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D76/1 and D76/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's about time for the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn and continue tomorrow at 14.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
